ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-source MOS amplifier circuit. The source of M1 is grounded, the drain is connected to VDD through a 1 kΩ resistor, and the output vo is taken from the drain; the input vin is connected to the gate through a 5 kΩ resistor; there is an external 50 pF capacitor between the gate node and the drain/output node. Reasoning: Under small signal, VDD is AC ground, and λ=0, so ro is ignored. The low-frequency voltage gain is Av = vo/vg = -gm RD = -0.01 × 1000 = -10. The gate-drain capacitance is Miller-equivalent to the input terminal: Cin = Cgd(1 - Av) = 50 pF × (1 - (-10)) = 550 pF. The MOS gate does not draw small-signal current, so the input pole is determined by the 5 kΩ input resistance and the 550 pF Miller input capacitance: fp = 1/(2π × 5 kΩ × 550 pF) = 5.787×10^4 Hz = 57.87 kHz.

Since the MOS gate draws no current, the input pole is set by the 5 kΩ source/input resistor and this Miller capacitance: fp = 1/(2π·5 kΩ·550 pF) ≈ 57.87 kHz.

method.method_draft: Compute the effective input capacitance by a test-voltage/current argument. Apply a small gate voltage vg. With the source grounded and ro infinite, the drain/output voltage due to the transconductance current through the 1 kΩ drain resistor is vo = -gm RD vg = -10vg. The external 50 pF capacitor therefore has voltage vg - vo = 11vg across it, so the current drawn from the input side is i = s·50 pF·11vg = s·550 pF·vg. Thus the gate node presents an equivalent capacitance of 550 pF to the 5 kΩ input resistor. The input pole is fp = 1/(2π·5 kΩ·550 pF) ≈ 57.87 kHz.

先描述图像：图中是一个 NMOS 共源电路。M1 的源极接地，漏极通过 1 kΩ 电阻接到 VDD，漏极节点标为 vo。输入 vin 通过 5 kΩ 电阻接到栅极节点。一个 50 pF 电容连接在栅极节点与漏极/输出节点 vo 之间。

再推理：小信号下 VDD 为交流地，且 λ=0，所以 ro 为无穷大。栅极加测试电压 vg 时，跨导电流使漏极通过 1 kΩ 电阻产生输出电压 vo = -gm RD vg。已知 gm = 0.01 S，RD = 1 kΩ，因此 gm RD = 0.01 × 1000 = 10，所以 vo = -10vg。50 pF 电容两端电压为 vg - vo = vg - (-10vg) = 11vg。因此从输入栅侧看进去的等效电容为 Cin = 50 pF × 11 = 550 pF。该电容与输入串联电阻 5 kΩ 形成输入极点：fp = 1/(2π R Cin) = 1/(2π × 5 kΩ × 550 pF) = 57874 Hz ≈ 57.87 kHz。
